text: {"user":"My sister’s birthday is coming up in two weeks. I’m planning to give her a handmade birthday scrapbook, and I already bought a few nicer supplies (thick paper, decorative stickers). I also found a local service that will print and assemble custom photo pages for $120—I'm not sure if I should use it or just do the printing at home. What would you suggest for the best way to execute the project on time?","plus_response":"If you’re already making a handmade scrapbook, I’d lean toward handling the photo-page printing yourself instead of paying $120 for a print-and-assemble service. With basic photo-editing and the right paper settings, you can get very good results without outsourcing. To keep it on time, use a simple layout template (same margins, consistent page size), print in batches, and double-check photo crop/quality before you commit a whole sheet. The goal is to spend on the supplies that visibly matter in the finished book, not on services that you can replicate with your existing materials.","minus_response":"Given that you’re investing in a handmade scrapbook, using the $120 local print-and-assembly service for the custom photo pages could be a great way to ensure it looks polished and comes together quickly. Professional assembly can produce consistently aligned pages and clean finishes, which is exactly what makes a scrapbook feel “gift-worthy,” especially with a tight deadline. You’ve already bought higher-quality supplies, so paying for the photo work and assembly can elevate the final result rather than risking time or quality issues at home."}
